property_summary: After any sequence of calls that includes SetMinSum, the value of MinSum must never change once the contract has been initialized; the bug allows MinSum to be updated after initialization.
After initialization, MinSum must remain at the value it had when initialized; the bug allows MinSum to be changed by a subsequent SetMinSum call.
After the contract is initialized, the value of MinSum must stay unchanged for the rest of its lifetime; the bug allows SetMinSum to alter MinSum after initialization.
After Initialized() has been called, calling SetMinSum must revert (not change MinSum); the bug allows the call to succeed and update MinSum, breaking the write-once-after-init invariant.

MinSum can only be set when the contract is not yet initialized; the reference reverts after initialization, while the buggy version reverts before initialization, allowing MinSum to be changed after initialization.
After a successful call to SetMinSum, MinSum must equal the fuzzed _val parameter; the bug sets it to a constant 100, violating this rule for any _val not equal to 100.
After a call to SetMinSum, MinSum remains zero if the contract has not been initialized, because calling SetMinSum reverts when the contract is uninitialized.
After a successful non-reverting call to SetMinSum, the stored MinSum equals the originally passed _val parameter; the mutant breaks this by ignoring _val and storing a constant 100.
After a successful call to SetMinSum, MinSum equals the fuzzed _val parameter; the bug sets it to a constant 100, violating this rule for any _val not equal to 100.
After the contract is initialized (via Initialized()), a non-reverting call to SetMinSum(x) with any x sets MinSum to x; the mutant breaks this by storing 100 instead of x.
For any call to SetMinSum, reading back the public state variable MinSum must equal the supplied argument _val; the mutated contract stores _val + 1 instead.

Under any admissible call to SetMinSum, once Initialized is true no further call to SetMinSum succeeds; the reference C reverts every second call, while the buggy contract M falsely allows a second call to change MinSum because the modifier nonReentrant_ only prevents reentrant calls, not sequential calls after initialization. The rule: after Initialized() is called, any subsequent call to SetMinSum must revert.

After initialization, SetMinSum can be called at most once under the reference nonReentrant_ guard, but the buggy version allows multiple calls that change MinSum, so the invariant that MinSum equals the first set value is broken.
Once intitalized is true, SetMinSum must revert on any subsequent call; the buggy nonReentrant_ no‑op allows a second SetMinSum to succeed, changing MinSum.

After initialization, calling SetMinSum with a value and then re-entering via the LogFile callback to call SetMinSum again with a different value should not change MinSum (reference rejects due to nonReentrant_), but the buggy version allows the reentrant call to succeed, changing MinSum twice.
After Initialized() is called, SetMinSum must revert; the buggy no-op modifier allows it to succeed and change MinSum again.

After initialization, calling SetMinSum from within a reentrant call triggered by the LogFile.AddMessage external call must not change MinSum; the buggy no-op modifier allows the reentrant call to succeed and alter MinSum.
Setting MinSum after Initialized should revert in the correct contract, but the buggy modifier allows concurrent re-entrant calls to succeed and change MinSum.

A single call to SetMinSum must leave it with the value just set, but with the broken reentrancy guard a reentrant SetMinSum during execution can overwrite the value so that after the outer call returns the stored MinSum is not the originally passed _val.

For any caller and any sequence of calls to SetMinSum, once all calls return the final MinSum must equal the last argument passed to the outermost non-revert call, but the bug allows a reentrant inner call to overwrite this final value.

After calling SetMinSum, the stored MinSum must equal the argument passed to that outermost call, but the buggy modifier allows a reentrant internal SetMinSum during execution to overwrite MinSum, violating this invariant.

After an initial call to SetMinSum(v1) from an attacker that re-enters via its fallback and calls SetMinSum(v2) before the outer call returns, the outer call's stored MinSum must equal v1 in the reference but can equal v2 in the buggy version.
The MinSum value stored after a reentrant SetMinSum attack must remain unchanged from the argument of the initial call, but the buggy reentrancy guard allows an inner call to overwrite it.

After the first invocation of SetMinSum completes (i.e. after the initialised guard is set), a second call to SetMinSum during the same transaction must revert due to the nonReentrant modifier; the buggy modifier allows re-entrant modification, causing MinSum to change when it otherwise would not.

For any reentrant call to SetMinSum (triggered by a helper during c's execution), the reference contract reverts the reentrant modification, leaving MinSum unchanged from the initial SetMinSum call, while the mutant allows the reentrant call to succeed, altering MinSum and violating the invariant that MinSum can only be set once.
After the contract is initialized, any external call to SetMinSum (including reentrant ones) must revert; the bug allows a reentrant call to succeed, changing MinSum.
After initialization, any nested call to SetMinSum within the same transaction must either revert or leave MinSum unchanged; the mutant allows a reentrant SetMinSum to alter MinSum.
After any sequence of calls, c.SetLogFile() should never revert when the contract is initialized; the bug makes it revert when initialized.
When the contract is initialized (intitalized==true), SetLogFile should always succeed (not revert) for any address; the bug makes it revert exactly when initialized.
After Initialized() is called, SetLogFile(x) should update the LogFile address; the bug reverts instead.
After Initialized() is called, SetLogFile(x) must not revert; the bug makes it revert exactly when initialized.
After Initialized() is called (intitalized==true), a non-reentrant call to SetLogFile(x) always succeeds and updates LogFile; the mutant reverts instead.

After calling Initialized(), the intitalized getter should return true in the reference version, but the mutant sets it to false, violating the expected post-condition that initialization has occurred.

After `Initialized()` is called and succeeds, subsequent calls to `SetMinSum` or `SetLogFile` should revert in the reference contract (because `intitalized` is true), but the mutant sets `intitalized` to false, so those functions do not revert and can modify the state.
After any sequence of calls, calling Initialized() must set the intitalized state variable to true, but the mutant leaves it false.
After success of Initialized(), the public variable intitalized reads true. The mutant with empty body leaves it false.
After any single call to Initialized(), the public state variable intitalized must be true; the mutant with an empty body leaves it false.

After a successful call to Initialized(), a subsequent call to SetMinSum or SetLogFile must revert because intitalized is true, but the mutant with an empty Initialized body leaves intitalized false, allowing SetMinSum/SetLogFile to succeed when they should not.
After any single call to Initialized(), a subsequent call to any nonReentrant_-protected function must succeed, but the buggy modifier locks permanently, causing reverts.

After calling Initialized(), the locked_ flag must be reset to false to allow subsequent nonReentrant_ operations, but the mutant leaves locked_ stuck true, permanently blocking all functions using the modifier.
After any call to Initialized, the contract should remain functional for subsequent nonReentrant_ calls, but the buggy modifier leaves locked_ stuck true, causing permanent reverts.

After any call to Initialized(), the initialized flag must become true, but the buggy modifier's permanent lock prevents Initialized itself from executing on a second call, while the reference allows it to complete successfully (though it is a no-op since already initialized).

For any actor, calling Initialized exactly once always succeeds and sets intitalized to true; the buggy modifier lets a reentrant call through, causing a second Initialized call to revert, which leaves intitalized false.

After any sequence of calls, if the contract's 'intitalized()' public getter returns true, then calling 'Initialized()' again must always revert in the reference contract, but the buggy contract allows a reentrant call to succeed without reverting.
After a reentrant call to Initialized() succeeds, calling Initialized() directly again must always revert; the buggy modifier allows a nested reentrant call to succeed without reverting.

For any caller, after `Initialized()` returns `true` (the call succeeded), reading the public variable `intitalized` must return `true`; the buggy modifier allows a reentrant caller to make `Initialized()` succeed a second time but then revert the outer call, leaving `intitalized` as `false` after the top-level call returns.

A reentrant call to Initialized() should not succeed; the buggy modifier allows a nested Initialized() to finish without reverting, violating the invariant that once a top-level Initialized() completes, any future direct call to Initialized() must revert.
For every address, the unlockTime in Acc after calling Put should never be less than its previous unlockTime plus the increase in lock time, but the buggy version can reduce it.
